paragraphs.source_en: Hataro was ordinarily as delicately beautiful as a woman, but once clad in armor he became another person entirely, every inch a soldier. The armor, even its visor, was forged entirely from pure Western iron. He hid the splendid clothes he had removed inside an old wooden barrel. A long spear lay amid the fishing nets and bundles of thatch in a corner of the hut. He thrust a keen blade behind his back, replacing the slender, ornate sword he had been holding.

paragraphs.source_en: Nobunaga had expected Motoyasu to attack Odaka Castle before the rainy season, but Motoyasu had deliberately waited until it was over; after entering Odaka Castle, he had swiftly withdrawn his troops, and when battle seemed imminent, he had extricated himself brilliantly from the ambush. For that very reason, he had ordered the palanquin bearers to hurry, reached Higashiura with all speed, and asked a local man of influence, Senda Sobei, to arrange lodgings.
